subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.
reasoning:
I'm designing the baku as a Japanese chimera combining tapir trunk, elephant tusks, tiger paws, ox tail, and rhino eyes, rendered in ukiyo-e style with flat indigo, vermilion, cream tones and black outlines with wave motifs, keeping the module compact and structurally sound.

I'm sketching the quadruped skeleton: body roughly 1.6m long and 1.3m at the shoulder, with legs built from limb IK chains running from hip joints down to foot points, a spine chain of catmull points curving from hips to chest, and a neck chain extending forward and up toward the head where the tapir-like trunk and tusks will attach.

For the body surface, I'm planning a loft over the hip-to-spine bone chain, with a two-tone coloring scheme referencing real tapirs—dark indigo at the front and rear with a cream middle band—though I'm unsure whether the loft options support banded coloring the way sweep does, so I may need a different approach for the color pattern.

I'll handle this with a custom paint function instead, checking position along the body to decide between cream and indigo for a wavy saddle-band effect. Given the "flat colour" constraint, I'll mostly stick to solid flat colors but allow a few paint-based gradients for the body's countershading and maybe a seigaiha wave motif, skipping hand-drawn outlines in favor of just bold ukiyo-e-style flat colors like a deep indigo.

I'm settling on a color palette (prussian blue, vermilion, cream, ink, gold, pale blue) and planning the surface details: cloud-shaped mane elements along the neck and back in cream and vermilion evoking flame/dream motifs, tiger-stripe sectors on the legs, and small stuck lathe discs forming concentric wave-ring patterns on the flanks to suggest seigaiha waves.

I'm defining facial and limb features — tapir-style trunk, large round rhino-like eyes with gold irises, cream-rimmed round ears, an ox-style tail with a flame tuft, and tiger-like paws with clawed toes.

Now I'm working out the body geometry in code, setting up mirrored left/right construction and loft stations along the torso with specific positions, widths, and heights to shape the body and determine where the hip joints and legs attach.

I'm working out the hind leg kinematics with three bending segments to get a digitigrade stance, checking total reach against the hip-to-foot distance, and naming the joint chain points (hip, knee, hock, paw) to match the limb's segments.

For the front legs, I'm using two segments bending backward at the elbow, naming them shoulder/elbow/paw, and verifying the reach distance works for the target foot position. Then I'm figuring out the parent joint hierarchy, connecting hind legs to the hips and front legs to the spine.

Now I'm setting up the leg geometry with tapered radii for a thicker thigh, and applying tiger-style ink stripes along the legs for color. For the paws, I'm planning simple sphere shapes for toes at the foot tips.

Using the last leg joint as the tip bone, then moving to the neck: I'm setting up a tapered sweep with three points rising from the shoulders to the head, naming the two spans neck1 and neck2, with the head joint anchored at the top point.

Now I'm moving on to the skull itself, lofting a tapering shape from the back of the head to the snout with decreasing width and height, then adding a lower jaw as a separate frustum shape positioned beneath it, angled slightly forward from a jaw joint.

Finishing the trunk path with a slight upward curl, parented to the head bone, naming segments trunk1 through trunk3 with the tentacle role. I'm adding a small cream ivory cap at the nostril tip, then sketching ivory tusk spikes curving from the jaw and snout using beveled sweeps.

Now I'm placing the eyes on the skull sides — a cream sphere base, a gold iris set slightly forward, and an ink pupil — working out the x-position relative to the skull's half-width at that height so they sit correctly on the surface.

I'm also adding vermilion eyebrow rods above them, then shaping the ears as flattened cylinders with a larger cream rim ring behind, positioned toward the top-rear of the head.

For the mane, I'm planning kumo-style flame extrusions running along the top and back of the neck, defining a 2D swirl outline for each flame and extruding it forward-facing, placed along the neck's curve at offset points above its radius.

I'm layering alternating colors (vermilion, cream, gold) by overlapping flames of different sizes and thicknesses so smaller ones poke through the bigger ones, with extra flame rows positioned along the spine's top.

For the back, I'm matching loft station positions to spine points raised by half the body height, then adding a cream saddle band painted onto a middle region of the body.

For the seigaiha pattern, I'm planning to embed small concentric ring discs on both flanks using raycasts from either side, alternating Prussian blue, cream, and vermilion colors for the stacked rings.

Now working out the ox tail: a short chain of segments curving down from the hips with decreasing sweep radii, ending in a tuft made of a few flame-shaped extrusions in vermilion and cream clustered at the tip.

Checking the tail tip rests above the floor, then moving on to the body's rear and the spine chain starting from the hips joint.

Now setting up the head joint attached to the end of the neck chain, with a jaw joint hinged below it for the mouth, and deciding to skip teeth, nostrils, and whiskers for simplicity.

I'm adding spiral gold cloud-curl flourishes on the shoulder and haunch for decoration, positioning them to sit outside the existing color bands, then moving on to set up an eye glow effect.

Now I'm planning the ground placement so paws sit at y=0, setting ear directions, and working out leg and paw positioning for the feet based on target coordinates and limb tip heights.

Still writing claw and toe geometry...

Dropping the sharp-point typing complication and just using plain smoothed points instead. Now I'm working out the mane placement along the neck curve — sampling points at intervals, extruding flame-like tufts outward and upward with decreasing size toward the head, alternating vermillion and cream colors for visual layering.

Adding smaller back flames along the spine, a forehead crest flame between the ears, and glowing iris colors on the eyes. For the body paint, I'm defining a paint function that returns a color string based on position, keeping unused parameters trailing so the signature stays simple while producing a cream color band.

I'm positioning the lower jaw box beneath the skull stations so it sits flush with the chin, closing the mouth gap, and fixing the mane point calculations to use the chain point's x/y/z coordinates properly before writing the final code.
